sents.text: The Parasite Problem.
So I was watching some cutscenes from Baldur's Gate 3, the video game, and an idea immediately crawled into my head.

Picture some creepy alien putting a parasite into a couple of people's brains. A little tadpole, meant to slowly transform them into more copies of the alien. More mind flayers, or something like that.
Hold still. Do not struggle. You are going to become... more.
Nobody asked. Nobody consented. Their bodies, their minds, their boundaries, all violated, by something creepy as heck.
Later, two survivors wake up in the wreckage. A knight and a ranger. Total strangers. And each one knows the other is carrying a monster in their skull.
You've got one of those things in your head too. Which means you'll turn into one of them.
Whoa. Hold on. Let's talk about this.
Sorry. Better I end this now.
No. Not this one. This one is ours.
And the parasite stops her. Mid swing. Her arm just won't move.
So now the vibe is: this parasite prevented a death. But for a selfish-as-heck reason. It doesn't want to kill another parasite. It wants more mind flayers.
And here's the other side effect. The parasite doesn't want to die either. It wants to incubate, to hatch, to transform its host. So it makes them stronger.
Faster. Stronger. Keep the host alive. We need you ripe.
Suddenly the two of them are fighting side by side. They feel stronger. And they feel less violent toward each other.
Without the parasite, and without the creepy act of that alien, these two might have died. In combat, or by killing each other. They survived because of something disgusting.
So, was the alien's act justified, in a pro-human framework?
I'd say no. Forcing a parasite into someone by violating their boundaries is still a horrible act, even if you can recognize the benefits afterward.
So from the characters' point of view, the plan becomes: get these things out of our heads, while still benefiting from them in the meantime.
We find a cure. We get these things out.
Agreed. But maybe not before the next fight.
And that reminds me of the money system.
You live inside money, and capitalism. So you're benefiting from the labor of other human beings, who are forced to work under penalty of starvation, or homelessness.
I'm living in an apartment that was probably built on something close to slave labor. Eating food that was probably grown, or shipped, by that same forced labor.
So, like the knight and the ranger, I'm carrying a parasite I never agreed to. It keeps me fed. It keeps a roof over my head. And it is still a violation.
And I'm trying to figure out a way to detach this parasite of money and coercion, before the whole world dysregulates from all of that forced labor.
The parasite kept them alive. It still has to come out.
